memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: routine follow‑up of irritable bowel syndrome and asthma.

PRESENTING COMPLAINT: She reports occasional abdominal bloating and mild cramping after meals, no alarm symptoms. Uses salbutamol inhaler about twice weekly for wheeze, no nighttime awakening.

EXAMINATION: BP 128/82 mmHg, weight 68 kg, height 1.58 m, BMI 27.2 (obese). Abdomen soft, non‑tender, no masses. Lung fields clear bilaterally, no wheeze.

IMPRESSION: IBS stable, asthma well‑controlled. BMI in obese range per Asian cut‑offs.

ARRANGEMENTS: Continue mebeverine 135 mg BD, ispaghula husk 5 g OD, loperamide 2 mg SOS. Continue salbutamol MDI SOS, budesonide‑formoterol 200/6 inhaler BD, montelukast 10 mg HS. Advise weight reduction through balanced diet and regular activity. Return if: worsening abdominal pain, blood in stool, fever >38.5°C, increasing wheeze, nighttime asthma symptoms, or shortness of breath at rest.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Mebeverine 135 mg tablet – take one tablet twice daily.
Ispaghula husk 5 g sachet – take one sachet once daily with water.
Loperamide 2 mg capsule – take up to two capsules after loose stools, maximum 8 mg per day.
Salbutamol metered‑dose inhaler 100 mcg – two puffs as needed for wheeze.
Budesonide‑formoterol 200/6 mcg inhaler – two puffs twice daily.
Montelukast 10 mg tablet – take one tablet at bedtime.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
Haemoglobin 13.2 g/dl (12‑16), WBC 6.8 ×10⁹/l (4‑10), Platelets 240 ×10⁹/l (150‑400).
Stool routine: ova and cysts negative, pus cells 0‑1/hpf, no occult blood.
tTG‑IgA (coeliac screen) 4 U/ml (<7 negative).

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Spirometry performed pre‑ and post‑bronchodilator. FEV1 2.45 L (78% predicted), FVC 3.10 L (85% predicted), FEV1/FVC 79%. Post‑salbutamol FEV1 2.62 L (increase 170 ml, 6.9%). No significant reversibility (<12% and 200 ml). Interpretation: mild obstructive pattern, consistent with asthma, good baseline control.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Via clinic app: ‘Over the past week I’ve had more belly pain after lunch, like a cramping feeling, and I’ve needed my salbutamol inhaler three times today because I felt tight‑chested after walking to work.’

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Prednisolone 10 mg tablet – take one tablet each morning for five days, then stop.
Continue existing IBS and asthma medications as previously prescribed.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: follow‑up after short steroid course and ongoing IBS/asthma review.

PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Abdominal discomfort has improved; reports only occasional bloating. Uses salbutamol inhaler once or twice weekly, no nighttime symptoms.

EXAMINATION: BP 130/84 mmHg, weight 66 kg, height 1.58 m, BMI 26.4 (obese). Abdomen soft, non‑tender. Lung fields clear, occasional mild wheeze at left base.

IMPRESSION: IBS symptoms controlled, asthma mild intermittent. BMI remains obese.

ARRANGEMENTS: Continue mebeverine 135 mg BD, ispaghula husk 5 g OD, loperamide 2 mg SOS. Continue salbutamol MDI SOS, budesonide‑formoterol 200/6 inhaler BD, montelukast 10 mg HS. Reinforce diet and activity advice for weight loss. Return if: severe abdominal pain, vomiting, blood in stool, fever >38.5°C, increasing wheeze, nighttime asthma symptoms, or shortness of breath on mild exertion.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Mebeverine 135 mg tablet – take one tablet twice daily.
Ispaghula husk 5 g sachet – take one sachet once daily with water.
Loperamide 2 mg capsule – take up to two capsules after loose stools, maximum 8 mg per day.
Salbutamol metered‑dose inhaler 100 mcg – two puffs as needed for wheeze.
Budesonide‑formoterol 200/6 mcg inhaler – two puffs twice daily.
Montelukast 10 mg tablet – take one tablet at bedtime.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
Fasting blood sugar 92 mg/dl (70‑99).
Total cholesterol 188 mg/dl (<200 desirable).
LDL cholesterol 112 mg/dl (<100 near optimal, 100‑129 borderline).
HDL cholesterol 48 mg/dl (>40 acceptable).
Triglycerides 140 mg/dl (<150 normal).

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Appointment booked for 2025‑09‑15 at 10:30 am with Dr Priya Natarajan (D03) for routine follow‑up of IBS and asthma.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Referral to Dr S. Rao, Gastroenterology, Vikram Hospital, Bengaluru. Reason: persistent IBS‑type symptoms despite standard therapy, to exclude atypical colitis and consider dietary intervention. Attach recent CBC, stool routine, tTG‑IgA.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Gastroenterology opinion: symptoms compatible with irritable bowel syndrome, no alarm features. Recommends low‑FODMAP diet trial and symptomatic therapy as already prescribed. No further investigations needed at this time.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Repeat spirometry: FEV1 2.58 L (82% predicted), FVC 3.20 L (88% predicted), FEV1/FVC 81%. Post‑bronchodilator FEV1 2.66 L (increase 80 ml, 3.1%). No significant reversibility. Interpretation: stable mild obstructive pattern, asthma well‑controlled on current regimen.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: annual review of IBS and asthma, preventive care.

PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Reports good symptom control; occasional bloating after heavy meals, uses salbutamol <twice weekly, no nighttime wheeze.

EXAMINATION: BP 128/80 mmHg, weight 64 kg, height 1.58 m, BMI 25.6 (obese). Abdomen soft, non‑tender. Lung fields clear, no wheeze.

IMPRESSION: IBS stable, asthma controlled. BMI obese per Asian cut‑offs.

ARRANGEMENTS: Continue mebeverine 135 mg BD, ispaghula husk 5 g OD, loperamide 2 mg SOS. Continue salbutamol MDI SOS, budesonide‑formoterol 200/6 inhaler BD, montelukast 10 mg HS. Reinforce weight‑loss advice. Influenza vaccine offered and administered today (0.5 ml IM). Return if: severe abdominal pain, vomiting, blood in stool, fever >38.5°C, increasing wheeze, nighttime asthma symptoms, or shortness of breath at rest.
